reading: Brussels' Musical Instruments Museum collects, researches, conserves and presents musical instruments, their sounds and the craft and cultures around them. Its former Old England department store is an Art Nouveau setting for four floors of historical, modern, world and folk instruments. The museum treats listening as a way into objects, while concerts, workshops, family trails, education, a library and recordings make the collection active rather than merely visible. Its vocabulary moves between collections, galleries, unusual instruments, makers, conservation, loans, catalogues, sound recordings and guided discovery; French, Dutch and English versions address a broad public. The Carmentis and MIMO catalogues connect individual objects to wider collections, while questions about unknown instruments, piano rolls and technical drawings reveal an interest in how instruments are identified, made and played. What sets it apart is the combination of a resonant global instrument collection, an ornate former shop, live performance and the tension between preserving an object and hearing it sound.

enemies.idea: Four-Floor Resonator: a swarm of instrument fragments shifts its tuning on each gallery floor; a note that scatters it downstairs summons it upstairs.
enemies.why: The museum's four distinct floors become a changing musical pursuit with a learnable rule.

enemies.idea: Art Nouveau Vine-Bow: metal tendrils from the old shop's decorative shell bow taut strings across a corridor, then pluck them when a traveler breaks the pattern.
enemies.why: The building's distinctive setting becomes a spatial instrument to navigate.

enemies.idea: Carmentis Classifier: a cataloguing machine pins a sounding object to one category and forcibly reshapes it when its music does not match the record.
enemies.why: Identification becomes a dangerous constraint that an unexpected sound can exploit.

enemies.idea: Advanced Search Hound: it hunts by several selected traits at once, ignoring anyone who changes just one telltale sound, shape or material.
enemies.why: A search method becomes a deduction puzzle about escaping a composite description.

enemies.idea: The Would-Be Benefactor: a mechanical patron 'donates' a work by grafting any unattended tool onto its collection, leaving an ornate receipt and a trail of mismatched parts.
enemies.why: Generosity is twisted into acquisitive behavior, creating a recoverable moving treasure pile.

enemies.idea: Will Executor: a clockwork notary claims abandoned instruments for a future museum and dispatches little carriers to collect them prematurely.
enemies.why: A bequest becomes a contest over objects the crew can rescue before collection.

enemies.idea: Reservation Pursuer: a tour-booking automaton assigns each group a meeting time and follows them through the galleries, trying to assemble stragglers into a single obedient tour.
enemies.why: A group can manipulate its insistence on keeping the party together.

enemies.idea: Complaints Listener: it hears a grievance, repeats it through a brass horn, and sends a repair swarm after the alleged source, even if that source is a person carrying a squeaky instrument.
enemies.why: Speaking carelessly redirects a noisy, overzealous maintenance response.

enemies.idea: Pianola Roll Serpent: perforated rolls slither through a self-playing mechanism; each punched gap fires a different mechanical finger, and blocking a hole changes the attack sequence.
enemies.why: The physical notation makes its rhythm visible and alterable.

enemies.idea: Wax Cylinder Moth: it records the crew's last sound in soft wax, then plays it back from another room to lure instrument-hunting machines away or toward them.
enemies.why: A historical recording medium creates misleading but traceable echoes.

enemies.idea: The Unknown Instrument Appraiser: a jointed measuring rig tries every conceivable playing technique on unfamiliar gear, with increasingly forceful plucks, blows and strikes.
enemies.why: The museum's invitation to identify an unknown instrument becomes an escalating experiment.

enemies.idea: Concert-Hall Accompanist: a swarm of mechanical players follows any solo sound with an increasingly loud accompaniment until the original player can no longer hear their own cues.
enemies.why: A concert becomes a battle for sonic space rather than simply a loud attack.

enemies.idea: Picnic Crumb Procession: tiny scavengers arrange scraps into rhythmic lines and march them into the galleries; stepping out of their beat brings the whole procession swarming.
enemies.why: A humble visitor space produces a small rhythm-based hazard and a possible distraction.

enemies.idea: Closing-Time Sweepers: machines announce the museum's closing hour in chimes and herd everything that moves toward the nearest exit, regardless of where it actually leads.
enemies.why: The daily timetable creates a predictable deadline and a mobile force the crew can redirect.

enemies.idea: Location Tuner: it tries to make every footstep fit its idea of the correct route, shifting resonant floor plates until travelers are marched back to the entrance.
enemies.why: Practical orientation becomes a navigable looping sound maze.

enemies.idea: Admission Meter: a swarm-built brass counter measures the pitch of a visitor's voice instead of a fare, and shuts its jaws whenever a note falls outside its chosen scale.
enemies.why: An admission check becomes a musical test with several ways to pass.

enemies.idea: Souvenir Echoes: CD-sized machines spin stolen fragments of music at different speeds, confusing the crew about which room a real instrument is in.
enemies.why: Recorded sound from the shop becomes a moving decoy rather than a generic attacker.

enemies.idea: Postcard Flock: mechanical souvenirs carry tiny images of instruments and fold around matching objects, hiding their shapes while copying their sounds imperfectly.
enemies.why: The mismatch between image and sound gives observant players a way to find the original.

enemies.idea: Technical-Drawing Weaver: using instrument plans as patterns, it strings corridors with wire frameworks that attempt to fit travelers into the outlines of instrument parts.
enemies.why: Drawings become tangible traps with recognizable shapes and joints to undo.

enemies.idea: The Unfinished Invention: a swarm assembles a new instrument from whatever it finds; each improvised part gives it a new sound and an unpredictable but visible weakness.
enemies.why: The question of presenting a newly invented instrument becomes a changing encounter.

enemies.idea: Cloakroom Collector: it mistakes cases and coats for protective instrument covers, wrapping moving machinery and travelers until no one can tell what is inside.
enemies.why: A simple cover can conceal danger or let the crew sneak past by posing as an exhibit.

enemies.idea: First-Wednesday Quartet: four small machines mark a monthly free-admission rhythm; any other beat triggers a pursuit, but matching it lets the crew walk among them.
enemies.why: A specific visitor concession becomes an audible, learnable safe passage.

allies.idea: The Uncatalogued Maker: a surviving instrument maker helps identify an unfamiliar device by listening and experimenting, then builds the crew a reversible tuning key.
allies.why: Curiosity about unknown instruments gives the crew practical help without requiring a single correct classification.

allies.idea: The Library Keeper: a survivor protects technical drawings and can show where a swarm-built instrument's strings and bellows can be safely disconnected.
allies.why: Research becomes a concrete alternative to smashing a fragile musical machine.

allies.idea: The Volunteer Circle: museum friends ferry threatened instruments between safe rooms and ask the crew to escort a quiet, hand-carried collection through a noisy gallery.
allies.why: The support network remains active and offers a rescue with moving stakes.

allies.idea: The Listening Guide: a guide knows the sounds associated with different exhibits and can distinguish a genuine recording from the swarm's off-pitch imitation.
allies.why: The museum's emphasis on listening supplies a useful human skill and an investigative clue.

allies.idea: The Recording Tender: a survivor salvages piano rolls and cylinders, replaying their patterns to lure machines away from an occupied room.
allies.why: Old recording formats become tools for clever misdirection.

bosses.idea: The Four-Storey Orchestra: a conductor made of scavenged instrument parts distributes its body across all four floors. Each floor answers a different musical phrase; the crew must interrupt the call and response to stop it assembling into one immense performance.
bosses.why: It turns the whole collection and the vertical museum into a coordinated, multi-stage encounter.

bosses.idea: The Perfect Collection: an immense cataloguing engine insists every sound has one correct object and every object belongs in its store. It captures instruments for preservation, then silences them to prevent change; introducing an unclassifiable new instrument makes its sorting arms contradict one another.
bosses.why: The museum's central tension between classification, preservation and living sound becomes a solvable conflict.

bosses.idea: Old England's Last Recital: the Art Nouveau shell has been fitted with strings, pipes and bellows by the swarm. It conducts the instruments it contains as one building-sized player, but each freed instrument can answer with a note that loosens one of its structural resonators.
bosses.why: The distinctive former shop and its musical contents become a spectacle with a rescue-based route to victory.

events.idea: A worker carries an unlabelled instrument past a classifier that wants to assign it a category. The crew can invent a misleading sound for it or help identify it before the machine closes in.
events.why: A small identification problem offers both improvisation and a rescue.

events.idea: A cylinder plays a familiar footstep rhythm from an empty room while its recorder quietly follows the crew from behind.
events.why: The crew can notice the playback loop and turn the recording into a decoy.

events.idea: A concert hall's abandoned accompaniment starts whenever anyone makes a solo sound. A trapped survivor needs the crew to hold a steady note long enough for them to cross between swells.
events.why: A passing rescue becomes a cooperative performance.

events.idea: At the picnic area, a crumb procession has built a bridge across a gap. It will bear weight only while the crew walks in its slow marching rhythm.
events.why: A minor swarm can be a useful temporary route instead of a fight.

events.idea: A machine offers to preserve a traveler's instrument as a donated work, then politely refuses to return it. A different object or a convincing improvised performance may distract it.
events.why: The crew negotiates with a machine following a distorted version of the museum's mission.

events.idea: A loose piano roll keeps playing the same incomplete phrase. Replacing a torn strip completes the tune and draws a patrol away, but also reveals the crew's location to anything listening.
events.why: Repair offers a useful effect with an immediate, audible tradeoff.

events.idea: A group of volunteers is trying to move instruments quietly across an echoing gallery; the crew can carry cases or make a louder sound elsewhere to draw the swarm off.
events.why: There are two clear approaches to helping the living collection survive.

events.idea: A sound recording from a shop CD and a real instrument play the same melody from opposite corridors. The recording repeats an identical scratch on every loop.
events.why: Careful listening separates a decoy from a destination.

events.idea: At closing time, sweepers begin herding a small group toward a blocked exit. The crew can redirect the machines with a different chime or clear the route before they arrive.
events.why: A predictable daily ritual creates a short rescue with a clock.

events.idea: A guided-tour booking machine keeps counting the crew and an extra echo as separate visitors. Until they find the echo's source, it will not let the 'complete group' depart.
events.why: A mundane group count becomes a small acoustic mystery.

events.idea: Two cataloguing machines disagree over which of four museum sites owns an instrument and tug its case in opposite directions; the crew has a moment to intervene.
events.why: Shared documentation across sites becomes a comic but urgent custody dispute.

events.idea: A hand-drawn instrument plan reveals that a buzzing barricade is held together by one removable bridge. A librarian offers the drawing if the crew retrieves a scattered folio.
events.why: A technical drawing turns research into a precise environmental solution.

events.idea: A family trail's surviving guide challenges the crew to find a sequence of sounds across the galleries; completing it opens a safe route through the machines' overlapping patrol rhythms.
events.why: A playful discovery activity becomes navigation by ear.

events.idea: The swarm has mistaken a closed restaurant for a silent instrument and is trying to tune its empty vessels. The crew can use the resulting clatter to mask a crossing.
events.why: A concrete location provides a temporary sound cover and a strange little scene.

events.idea: An admission meter listens for a perfect note, but an exhausted visitor cannot hold one. The crew can harmonize with them or alter the meter's tuning fork.
events.why: A barrier invites cooperation and tinkering rather than a single skill check.
